title: AI Boards: Richer Structure, Better Tool Choice
excerpt: Canvio AI now builds more useful editable boards with varied objects, meaningful relations, stronger topic detail, and the language requested by the user.
takeaways: Generated boards can combine notes, text, shapes, code, maps when location matters, frames, and semantic relations instead of repeating one card type.
The assistant asks for all visible board text and relation labels in the user's requested language, including Arabic.
Topic-specific prompts encourage examples, evidence, misconceptions, questions, and next actions instead of generic headings.
After generation, Canvio reports what was created and clearly identifies when a local fallback was used.

sections.heading: A useful board is more than a stack of notes
paragraphs: Early AI drafts could produce a recognizable diagram but still feel repetitive. The improved generation contract asks for an editable reasoning board: a clear central idea, supporting evidence, a challenge or open question, a practical next action, and relations that explain how the parts connect.
The result is still a starting point, not a finished answer. Every object remains movable, editable, reconnectable, and available to the same tools as work created by hand.

sections.heading: The tool should match the idea
paragraphs: Canvio AI can choose sticky notes for short ideas, text for headings, shapes for decisions or concepts, code blocks for real technical examples, and Living Maps only when the topic is genuinely geographic. Frames keep the generated workspace together and fit it into view.
Semantic relations such as Depends on, Explains, Causes, Contradicts, and Leads to make the structure readable by people and by the Visual Reasoning Partner.

sections.heading: The board should speak the user's language
paragraphs: The generation flow now detects or accepts the requested output language and carries it through the server and local fallback. Visible node text and relation labels are requested in that language while the internal board schema stays stable.
This matters for real classrooms and teams. Someone can ask for an Arabic study board, a French project plan, or an English technical architecture without manually translating every generated card.

sections.heading: More transparent when the server is unavailable
paragraphs: A generated result now summarizes its object and relation mix so people can quickly understand what changed. If the hosted AI provider is unavailable or rate-limited, Canvio identifies the local smart fallback instead of quietly presenting it as a server response.
That keeps the workflow resilient while preserving trust: the board remains useful, and the user knows which reasoning path produced it.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Canvio's larger idea is connected visual knowledge work, not AI decoration. Better generation supports that vision by creating material people can question, reorganize, connect, present, and continue developing with the full whiteboard toolkit.

title: Visual Reasoning Partner: Score, Explain, Act
excerpt: A clearer reasoning score now explains what it measures and recommends the best next move for the board.
takeaways: The score is now based on five visible factors: connectedness, relation clarity, evidence grounding, logic safety, and reasoning depth.
A Best next move card turns the weakest factor into a focused action such as connecting loose ideas, labeling unclear links, or grounding unsupported claims.
AI audit, Challenge, and Socratic modes read the board graph instead of starting from a blank chat context.
Quick-Connect and semantic relation labels still keep the reasoning visible directly on the canvas.

sections.heading: A score needs to explain itself
paragraphs: A single health number is only useful when people can understand why it changed. The Reasoning Partner now breaks the board score into five factors: connectedness, relation clarity, evidence grounding, logic safety, and reasoning depth.

This makes the score easier to trust. A low score no longer feels like a vague warning. It shows whether the board needs more links, clearer relation labels, stronger evidence, safer logic, or deeper structure.

sections.heading: Best next move turns diagnosis into action
paragraphs: After the score is calculated, Canvio looks at the weakest factor and suggests one practical next step. If ideas are floating alone, it recommends connecting them. If links are unlabeled, it recommends clarifying relation meaning. If claims lack support, it recommends adding evidence.
The goal is not to grade the person using the board. The goal is to make a messy canvas easier to improve without forcing people to guess what to do next.

sections.heading: AI reads the board graph
paragraphs: The reasoning tools now pass a compact board summary to the assistant: visible nodes, relation labels, relation types, and map pin context where it exists. That helps the AI respond to the work on the board instead of giving a generic answer.
Challenge mode can look for weak assumptions. Socratic mode can ask better follow-up questions. Summary and article actions can use the current structure as source material.

sections.heading: Relations stay part of the canvas language
paragraphs: The board still uses the same direct interactions: quick-drag ports, typed labels, relation styles, and semantic relation types. The reasoning partner does not replace the canvas. It reads what people already built and helps them make it clearer.
This is important for everyday use. Students, teachers, researchers, and developers can keep thinking spatially while still getting useful feedback from the system.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Canvio is not trying to be another blank drawing surface. The larger idea is a visual knowledge workspace where objects, places, relations, and AI support the same thinking process.
A transparent score and a concrete next move bring that vision closer: the board can now help people understand their own structure, not only store it.

title: Laser Pointer: Guide Attention Without Marking the Board
excerpt: A temporary presentation tool for pointing at ideas during lessons, reviews, and live collaboration.
takeaways: The pointer follows mouse, touch, and pen input without creating a canvas object.
It can pass over notes, shapes, maps, and frames without moving or editing them.
Choose Laser Pointer from the toolbar or press Q, then return to Select when finished.

sections.heading: Point without leaving a mark
paragraphs: Teaching and presenting often require a quick gesture rather than a new object. The laser pointer lets someone direct attention to a word, relation, map pin, or visual detail without adding ink that must be erased later.
The pointer is temporary and is never stored in the board. Moving away or changing tools leaves the workspace exactly as it was.

sections.heading: Designed to stay out of the way
paragraphs: While Laser Pointer is active, canvas objects do not capture the gesture. That means the pointer can move across notes, shapes, maps, frames, and relations without accidentally selecting or dragging them.
The tool works with a mouse, touch input, or a tablet pen. Press Q for fast access, or choose Laser Pointer from the main toolbar when discoverability matters more than speed.

sections.heading: A presentation tool, not another drawing mode
paragraphs: The pointer is intentionally simple: it communicates “look here now” and then disappears. Permanent emphasis still belongs to ink, highlighter, arrows, relations, and focused board objects.

title: AI Navigator: Create, Study, Summarize, Article, and Tidy
excerpt: Why Canvio turns AI into board-aware actions instead of a generic chat window.
takeaways: AI drafts become normal, editable Canvio objects.
Five modes make the assistant easier to use: Create, Study, Summary, Article, and Tidy.
When a board already has content, AI uses notes, relation labels, relation types, and map pins as context.
Generated boards are fitted into view so people can start editing immediately.

sections.heading: The problem with generic AI answers
paragraphs: A useful idea can become difficult to use when it arrives as one long response. People need to compare parts, move them around, add evidence, and change the structure as they learn more.

Canvio treats AI as a starting partner for spatial thinking. The result is not a finished poster or a hidden chat answer. It is a first board, summary, article, or cleanup suggestion that people can question and reshape.

sections.heading: Five clearer ways to ask
paragraphs: The AI Navigator now starts with intent. Create helps turn a prompt into a board. Study helps explain and review a topic. Summary and Article use the current board as source material. Tidy focuses on improving structure.

This is easier than a blank prompt box because the user can choose the job before typing. It also keeps the assistant aligned with the main product idea: a visual board, not a separate chat experience.

sections.heading: The board becomes context
paragraphs: When a board already has content, Canvio sends the assistant a compact digest of the visible structure: notes, text, relation labels, relation types, and map pin labels. This helps AI respond to what is actually on the canvas.

A prompt can still create a frame, a central shape, supporting notes, and labeled relations. Those generated elements remain normal Canvio objects, so they can be edited, connected, presented, exported, or deleted like anything else on the canvas.
The AI flow also fits the created structure into view. That small step matters: a useful first draft should be visible immediately, not left somewhere off-screen.

sections.heading: The design principle
paragraphs: AI should reduce the blank-page problem without taking ownership away from the person thinking. Canvio keeps generated choices visible, editable, and connected to the board.

title: Relations: Turning Notes Into Connected Thinking
excerpt: A relation is more useful when it explains why two ideas belong together, not only that a line exists.
takeaways: Relations explain meaning such as cause, proof, sequence, and dependency.
Labels and routing keep important connections readable as boards change.
The same relation model works across notes, maps, shapes, and frames.

sections.heading: Lines are not enough
paragraphs: A plain line can show proximity, but it does not explain meaning. In a lesson, a research board, or a project plan, the important question is often whether one idea proves, enables, depends on, or leads to another.

sections.heading: Meaning stays attached
paragraphs: Canvio relations have labels, relationship types, colors, and editable endpoints. Routing responds to the objects around it so the connection can remain readable as the board changes.
The same interaction works across notes, shapes, frames, maps, and other living objects. That makes relations part of the workspace language rather than a special diagram mode.

sections.heading: A calmer visual system
paragraphs: The goal is not to put more lines on a board. It is to make the important connections easier to follow, especially when the board is being taught, reviewed, or shared with someone new.

title: Maps Are Optional in the Workflow, Native in the System
excerpt: Location is powerful when it matters. Canvio keeps maps native without making every board start from a map.
takeaways: Maps are optional for each board, not optional as a first-class Canvio object.
Relations can attach to exact pins, not only to the whole map object.
Pins can sit beside evidence, decisions, and notes on the same board.
The larger product remains a connected workspace for notes, relations, AI, frames, drawing, presentation, and research.

sections.heading: Optional for the workflow
paragraphs: A field visit, geography lesson, or site investigation may need a map. A study guide, architecture review, or decision board may not. Canvio starts with the task, so the board determines which objects matter.

sections.heading: Native when place matters
paragraphs: When a map is useful, pins can sit alongside notes, images, relations, and decisions. A location becomes part of the reasoning instead of a separate screen that people have to leave the board to inspect.

Relations can now point to individual pins, so a note can connect to a specific site visit, address, classroom example, or research location. That makes place feel native to the board without making every board about maps.

sections.heading: Part of the larger workspace
paragraphs: The same board can move from a concept map to a site view, then back to the larger story. Maps are one strong object inside a broader workspace for connected thinking, learning, planning, and research.
That is the product direction: Canvio is a connected whiteboard first, where maps, AI, relations, notes, frames, drawing, and presentation work together when the idea needs them.

title: Designing Canvio for Mouse, Touch, Tablet, and Pen
excerpt: Why direct manipulation needs different protections on a laptop, a tablet, and a small phone.
takeaways: Mouse, touch, and pen need different interaction protections.
Dedicated handles and clear active tools reduce accidental movement.
Undo, redo, fit view, and recovery are part of good touch design.

sections.heading: The canvas has more than one input
paragraphs: A mouse offers precision. A finger needs space. A pen expects drawing to feel immediate. The same board has to accept all three without making selection, panning, and editing fight each other.

sections.heading: Small details make the difference
paragraphs: Canvio uses larger touch targets, dedicated drag handles for notes, clearer active tools, and recovery controls such as undo, redo, and fit view. The interface should explain what is active without covering the work.

sections.heading: Designing for recovery
paragraphs: Good touch interaction is not only about preventing mistakes. It is also about making mistakes easy to reverse. Every device should let people try, move, zoom, and return to a useful view with confidence.

title: Private by Default: Keeping Workspace Data in Its Context
excerpt: A shared link should help the right people collaborate without turning personal board content into public search results.
takeaways: A shared board link does not mean a board should be searchable.
Workspace routes stay out of the public sitemap and search index.
The public website and private thinking space serve different jobs.

sections.heading: A board can contain unfinished thinking
paragraphs: Notes, research, decisions, and classroom plans are often useful before they are polished. People need a place to work privately, then choose when and how to share the result.

sections.heading: Sharing and discoverability are different
paragraphs: Canvio keeps workspace routes out of the public sitemap and marks them as non-indexable. That preserves direct sharing while avoiding the assumption that every board should appear in a search engine.

sections.heading: A product promise
paragraphs: The public website explains Canvio. The workspace is where people think. Keeping those contexts separate is a small technical choice with a large trust effect.
